forge/agents:
Agents reach Forge the same way you do: with a MIOSA API key, under the same organization roles and branch policy. Nothing an agent does can skip a policy that would stop you. ## From the TypeScript SDK ```bash npm install @miosa/sdk ``` ```ts import { Miosa } from "@miosa/sdk"; const miosa = new Miosa({ apiKey: process.env.MIOSA_API_KEY }); // Every repository in your organization. const repos = await miosa.forge.repositories.list(); console.log(repos.map((repo) => repo.name)); // Read a file from the default branch. const repo = repos.find((r) => r.slug === "hello-forge"); const file = await miosa.forge.repositories.blob(repo.id, { path: "public/index.html" }); console.log(file.content); ``` `miosa.forge.repositories` also has `create`, `get`, `refs`, `tree`, `readme`, `commits`, `putFile`, `deleteFile`, `update` and `delete`. The Python SDK has the same surface as `client.forge`. ## The REST API All routes are under `https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/forge/repositories` and take your key as `Authorization: Bearer `. `:id` is the repository id. | Method | Path | What it does | |---|---|---| | `GET` | `/` | List repositories | | `POST` | `/` | Create a repository | | `GET` | `/:id` | Show a repository | | `GET` | `/:id/refs` | Branches and tags | | `GET` | `/:id/tree?ref=main&path=` | A directory listing | | `GET` | `/:id/blob?ref=main&path=README.md` | A file's content | | `GET` | `/:id/commits?ref=main` | Commit history | | `POST` | `/:id/branches` | Create a branch: `{"name": "...", "from": "main"}` | | `PUT` | `/:id/files/:path` | Write a file as a commit on a branch | | `GET` | `/:id/pull-requests` | List pull requests | | `POST` | `/:id/pull-requests` | Open a pull request: `{"title", "head", "base"}` | | `POST` | `/:id/pull-requests/:number/reviews` | Review a pull request | | `POST` | `/:id/pull-requests/:number/merge` | Merge a pull request | | `POST` | `/:id/pull-requests/:number/close` | Close a pull request | | `GET` | `/:id/check-suites` | Checks reported against commits | | `GET` | `/:id/releases` | List releases | | `POST` | `/:id/releases` | Publish a release | > **Note: Every write needs an Idempotency-Key** > > Each `POST` and `PUT` needs an `Idempotency-Key` header. > Repeating a request with the same key returns the first result instead of acting twice, so an agent can retry safely. > Without the header the API answers `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`. ### Write a file to a branch A file write is a commit. It needs the branch's current head commit as `expected_head`, so two writers never overwrite each other silently: ```bash curl -X PUT "https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/forge/repositories/$REPO_ID/files/public%2Fapi.html" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"path\": \"public/api.html\", \"content\": \"

From the API.

\\n\", \"message\": \"Add a page from the API\", \"branch\": \"api-branch\", \"expected_head\": \"$HEAD_SHA\"}" ``` The answer has the new commit and the policy decision that allowed it. Without `expected_head` the API answers `EXPECTED_HEAD_REQUIRED`; get the head from `GET /:id/refs`.
forge/cli:
Every command takes a repository by name, `org/name` or id, except `repo show`, `repo update` and `repo delete`, which take the id.
Add `--json` to any command for a stable JSON envelope.
Commands that change something take `--idempotency-key`, so a retry never acts twice.

> **Note: Version**
>
> These examples use CLI 2.3.10.
> Run `miosa update` to get the latest.

## auth

| Command | Example |
|---|---|
| `auth setup-git` | `miosa forge auth setup-git` |

Makes git use your MIOSA key for `https://forge.miosa.ai`.
`--host` points it at another Forge host.

## repo

| Command | Example |
|---|---|
| `repo create` | `miosa forge repo create hello-forge --visibility private --default-branch main` |
| `repo list` | `miosa forge repo list` |
| `repo show` | `miosa forge repo show <repository-id>` |
| `repo clone` | `miosa forge repo clone hello-forge` |
| `repo update` | `miosa forge repo update <repository-id> --name "Hello Forge"` |
| `repo delete` | `miosa forge repo delete <repository-id> --yes` |

`repo create` also takes `--slug` and `--project-id`.
`repo delete` is permanent.

## pr

| Command | Example |
|---|---|
| `pr new` | `miosa forge pr new hello-forge --head greeting --title "Change the greeting"` |
| `pr list` | `miosa forge pr list hello-forge --state all` |
| `pr show` | `miosa forge pr show hello-forge 1` |
| `pr diff` | `miosa forge pr diff hello-forge 1 --name-only` |
| `pr comment` | `miosa forge pr comment hello-forge 1 --body "Looks good to me."` |
| `pr comments` | `miosa forge pr comments hello-forge 1` |
| `pr review` | `miosa forge pr review hello-forge 1 --decision approved --body "Ship it."` |
| `pr merge` | `miosa forge pr merge hello-forge 1` |
| `pr check` | `miosa forge pr check hello-forge 1 --name lint --conclusion passed --head-sha <sha> --file check.json` |
| `pr checkout` | `miosa forge pr checkout hello-forge 2 --branch review-2` |
| `pr close` | `miosa forge pr close hello-forge 2` |
| `pr reopen` | `miosa forge pr reopen hello-forge 2` |

`pr new` takes `--base`, `--body`, `--draft` and `--head-repo` for a pull request from a fork.
`pr list` filters with `--state open|closed|merged|all`, `--author` and `--base`.
`pr review --decision` is `approved`, `changes_requested` or `commented`.
`pr check` reports a check on the pull request's head commit and is refused for the pull request's own author.

## check

| Command | Example |
|---|---|
| `check report` | `miosa forge check report hello-forge --commit <sha> --name unit-tests --conclusion passed --file check.json` |
| `check list` | `miosa forge check list hello-forge --commit <sha>` |
| `check suite` | `miosa forge check suite hello-forge <sha>` |
| `check show` | `miosa forge check show hello-forge <check-id>` |
| `check evidence` | `miosa forge check evidence hello-forge <check-id>` |

A completed check needs `{"evidence": {...}}` in `--file`, up to 64 KB.
`--status queued` or `in_progress` reports a check that is still running.

## policy

| Command | Example |
|---|---|
| `policy show` | `miosa forge policy show hello-forge` |
| `policy set` | `miosa forge policy set hello-forge --approvals 1 --check unit-tests` |
| `policy owners` | `miosa forge policy owners hello-forge` |

See [branch policy](/docs/forge/pull-requests#branch-policy) for every flag.

## grant

| Command | Example |
|---|---|
| `grant set` | `miosa forge grant set hello-forge <user-id> --role write` |

Roles are `read`, `write`, `maintain` and `admin`.

## fork

| Command | Example |
|---|---|
| `fork` | `miosa forge fork hello-forge --name hello-forge-fork` |

## release

| Command | Example |
|---|---|
| `release tag` | `miosa forge release tag hello-forge --name v0.1.0 --message "First tag"` |
| `release new` | `miosa forge release new hello-forge --tag v0.1.0 --name "First release" --body "Hello from Forge."` |
| `release upload` | `miosa forge release upload hello-forge v0.1.0 --source-archive` |
| `release list` | `miosa forge release list hello-forge` |
| `release show` | `miosa forge release show hello-forge v0.1.0` |

`release new` creates the tag if it does not exist; `--commit` picks what it points at and `--prerelease` marks it.
`release upload` attaches files, or a `.tar.gz` of the tagged commit with `--source-archive`.
forge/faq:
## Are repositories private?

Yes, by default.
A repository is `private`, `internal` or `public`, set with `repo create --visibility` or changed later with `repo update`.
Members of your organization get access through their organization role, and `grant set` gives one person an extra role on one repository.

## Which permissions does my API key need?

`forge:read` to clone, fetch and read, and `forge:write` to push, open and merge pull requests, report checks and publish releases.
`miosa login` gives a key with both.
A key without them gets `insufficient scope` and the name of the permission it needs.

## Can I use the GitHub CLI or another Git host?

Forge speaks standard Git over HTTPS, so any Git client works once `miosa forge auth setup-git` has run.
Pull requests, checks, policy and releases use `miosa forge`, the API or the SDKs.

## Can I import a repository from GitHub?

Yes, from the console.
An import copies the history once; a GitHub App connection keeps a repository mirrored.

## What Forge does not do

| Not supported | What to do |
|---|---|
| Issues | Track work in your own tool, or in pull request comments |
| Repository secrets | Set them on the deployment with `miosa deploy env-set` |
| CI that runs on push | Run your tests elsewhere and report the result with `miosa forge check report` |
| Squash, rebase and auto merge | Merges create a merge commit; the server refuses the other methods without merging |
| Pushing from a sandbox with its own identity | See [Forge from a sandbox](/docs/forge/sandboxes) |
| Raw file download, blame and Git LFS | Clone the repository |

> **Note**
>
> Forge does not do these today.

## Why was my merge refused?

The pull request does not meet the branch policy yet, and nothing was merged.
The error names what is missing and the command that fixes it; see [Fix "needs approval"](/docs/forge/pull-requests#fix-needs-approval).
forge/pull-requests:
A pull request on a Forge repository works the way you expect from other Git hosts.
Checks report results against its commits, and branch policy decides when it can merge.

## Open a pull request

Push a branch, then open the pull request against the default branch:

```bash
git checkout -b greeting
sed -i.bak 's/Hello from Forge/Hello again from Forge/' public/index.html && rm public/index.html.bak
git commit -am "Change the greeting"
git push -u origin greeting
miosa forge pr new hello-forge --head greeting --title "Change the greeting" --body "Says hello again."
```

```text
Number:  1
Title:   Change the greeting
State:   open
From:    greeting
Into:    main
```

Read it back, see what changed and talk about it:

```bash
miosa forge pr list hello-forge
miosa forge pr show hello-forge 1
miosa forge pr diff hello-forge 1 --name-only
miosa forge pr comment hello-forge 1 --body "Looks good to me."
miosa forge pr comments hello-forge 1
```

## Branch policy

Branch policy decides what a pull request needs before it can merge into a branch.

```bash
miosa forge policy show hello-forge
```

```text
Policy:         main v1 (default policy)
Merging needs:  no approval needed (solo organization; the default policy tightens when a second member joins)
Approvals:      1
Independent:    yes
Self-merge:     yes
Checks:         none
```

An organization with one member merges without approvals.
Once a second person joins, the default policy asks for one approval from someone other than the author.

Set your own rules with `policy set`:

```bash
miosa forge policy set hello-forge --approvals 1 --check unit-tests
```

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--approvals N` | How many approvals a pull request needs |
| `--independent` | The approver must be someone other than the author (default on) |
| `--check NAME` | A check that must pass; repeat it for several |
| `--code-owners` | Require a code owner's approval |
| `--dismiss-stale` | New commits dismiss earlier approvals (default on) |
| `--branch NAME` | The branch the policy covers (default: the default branch) |

### Working alone

An organization with one member can turn off the approval requirement so the author merges their own pull requests:

```bash
miosa forge policy set hello-forge --branch main --approvals 0 --independent=false
```

Required checks still apply.

## Report your own checks

Any tool can report a check against a commit, for example a test run.
A completed check needs evidence: a JSON file with an `evidence` object of up to 64 KB.

```bash
echo '{"evidence": {"runner": "npm test", "passed": 12, "failed": 0}}' > check.json
miosa forge check report hello-forge --commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" --name unit-tests --conclusion passed --summary "12 tests passed" --file check.json
miosa forge check list hello-forge --commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
```

> **Note: A required check comes from someone else**
>
> A check that branch policy requires must be reported by someone other than the pull request's author: MIOSA itself, a CI identity or another member of your organization.
> That way an author can never pass their own gate.
> A check the author reports still shows on the pull request, but it does not count toward the policy, and `miosa forge pr check` refuses it with `CHECK_SEPARATION_REQUIRED`.

## Review and merge

A teammate reviews the pull request; the author cannot approve their own:

```bash
miosa forge pr review hello-forge 1 --decision approved --body "Ship it."
```

When the branch policy is met, anyone with write access merges it:

```bash
miosa forge pr merge hello-forge 1
```

```text
ok  Merged pull request #1 into main as 0d4d9eebbc76
```

> **Note: Merge methods**
>
> Today a merge always creates a merge commit.
> The CLI already has `--squash`, `--rebase` and `--auto`, but the server refuses them with `this MIOSA server does not support --squash yet; nothing was merged`.
> Nothing is merged when that happens.

## Fix "needs approval"

When a pull request does not meet its branch policy, the merge is refused and nothing changes:

```text
miosa: pull request #3 cannot merge: policy main v5 needs 1 approval from someone other than the author [REQUIRED_APPROVALS_MISSING]
  Ask someone with write access to approve:  miosa forge pr review hello-forge 3 --decision approved
  Working alone? Let the author merge:      miosa forge policy set hello-forge --branch main --approvals 0 --independent=false
```

Either ask a member with write access to approve, or, if you work alone, lower the policy with the second command.
A missing required check fails the same way with `REQUIRED_CHECK_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE`; run `miosa forge pr show` to see which check is missing.

## Work on someone else's pull request

```bash
miosa forge pr checkout hello-forge 2 --branch review-2
miosa forge pr close hello-forge 2
miosa forge pr reopen hello-forge 2
```
forge/quickstart:
This takes about five minutes. You need the `miosa` CLI (version 2.3.10 or later) and `git`. ## 1. Sign in ```bash miosa login miosa whoami ``` `miosa login` gives the CLI a key with the Forge permissions, `forge:read` and `forge:write`. If you use an API key you created yourself instead, tick both permissions when you create it under **API keys** in the console, then `export MIOSA_API_KEY=msk_...`. Without them every `miosa forge` command answers `insufficient scope`. ## 2. Let git use your MIOSA login ```bash miosa forge auth setup-git ``` ```text ok git now uses your MIOSA login for https://forge.miosa.ai ``` This adds a credential helper for `forge.miosa.ai` to your global git config. Git then signs in with your MIOSA key, so you never paste a password or token. ## 3. Create a repository and clone it ```bash miosa forge repo create hello-forge miosa forge repo clone hello-forge cd hello-forge ``` ```text ok Created repository "hello-forge" in the current organization Visibility: private Clone URL: https://forge.miosa.ai//hello-forge.git ``` A new repository is private and starts empty, so git warns that you cloned an empty repository. ## 4. Commit and push ```bash mkdir -p public printf '\nHello from Forge\n

Hello from Forge

\n' > public/index.html git add . git commit -m "First page" git push -u origin main ``` That is plain git: any client, editor or tool that speaks Git over HTTPS works the same way. ## 5. Open a pull request ```bash git checkout -b greeting sed -i.bak 's/Hello from Forge/Hello again from Forge/' public/index.html && rm public/index.html.bak git commit -am "Change the greeting" git push -u origin greeting miosa forge pr new hello-forge --head greeting --title "Change the greeting" miosa forge pr merge hello-forge 1 ``` ```text ok Merged pull request #1 into main as 0d4d9eebbc76 ``` An organization with one member can merge its own pull requests. Once a teammate joins, a pull request needs their approval first; see [branch policy](/docs/forge/pull-requests#branch-policy). ## Clean up ```bash miosa forge repo list miosa forge repo delete --yes ``` `repo delete` takes the repository id that `repo list` shows, and it is permanent. ## Next - [Pull requests, checks and branch policy](/docs/forge/pull-requests) - [Every forge command](/docs/forge/cli)
forge/sandboxes:
Code written inside a sandbox, by you or by an agent, should land in a Forge repository with a plain `git push`. No API key is copied into the sandbox for that. > **Note: Rolling out** > > Everything on this page is rolling out now. > Until it reaches your organization, a `git clone` or `git push` to Forge from inside a sandbox answers `Authentication failed`. ## How it works A sandbox already carries its own token, scoped to its organization and workspace. Forge accepts that token for the repositories of the sandbox's own workspace, and the sandbox writes a git credential helper for `forge.miosa.ai` when it boots. So inside the sandbox, git just works: ```bash git clone https://forge.miosa.ai//.git cd git checkout -b from-sandbox echo "

Written in a sandbox.

" >> public/index.html git commit -am "Edit from a sandbox" git push -u origin from-sandbox ``` The sandbox reaches only the repositories of its own workspace, with the same branch policy as everyone else. Then open a pull request from your machine, the CLI or the API, as in [pull requests](/docs/forge/pull-requests). ## Today, before it reaches you Do not copy a personal API key into a sandbox to work around it: anyone and any agent that can read the sandbox can read the key. If you need the files now, copy them out with `miosa files cp -r my-box:/workspace/site ./site` and push from your machine.
